bottom_line: The Fed (the people who set interest rates) released notes from its October meeting showing almost all officials expect to raise rates again, because prices are still rising too fast. That pushed the dollar to a 19-month high and weighed on stocks, even as Wall Street gets ready for Anthropic's record stock market debut.

stories.title: Fed says more rate hikes coming
stories.real: The Fed held its key rate in a range of 3.75%-4% in October, but its meeting notes show almost all officials expect more hikes, with December in view and some wanting a bigger one. Fed governor Waller even said they may need to 'shock' people with a half-point hike.
stories.you: Loans, credit cards and mortgages could get more expensive, while savings accounts may pay a bit more.

stories.title: Anthropic's record-breaking stock debut
stories.real: Anthropic, the five-year-old AI company behind Claude, raised $81.3 billion by selling shares at $83 each, the largest stock offering on record, topping SpaceX. It starts trading on the Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT, valued at up to $1.5tn, and regular investors are very excited about it.
stories.you: Hype around a brand-new stock can make its price swing wildly, so anyone looking at it should understand that before putting money in.

stories.title: Nvidia's strong results didn't calm nerves
stories.real: Nvidia posted strong earnings, but its shares slipped anyway, with worries about who leads the company after Jensen Huang's exit and about its China business. Fears about how much debt AI companies like CoreWeave and Oracle are carrying are running high.
stories.you: If you own tech or AI-heavy funds, good news from one company isn't settling the bigger worry about AI spending and debt.

stories.title: UK prices and energy bills rising
stories.real: Record diesel prices pushed UK inflation (how fast prices rise) to a one-year high of 3.6%. A typical household energy bill is forecast to go up by £443 a year from January, a 26% jump, driven by high wholesale gas prices.
stories.you: For UK households, heating and everyday costs are about to take a bigger bite out of the budget.

stories.title: Australia loses jobs after rate hikes
stories.real: Australia's economy shed 43,500 jobs and unemployment jumped to 4.9%, a four-year high, after its central bank (the RBA) raised rates.
stories.you: It's a real example of how higher interest rates can cool an economy by costing people jobs.
